verses.zh: 利未的曾孙、哥辖的孙子、以斯哈的儿子可拉，和流便子孙中以利押的儿子大坍、亚比兰，与比勒的儿子安，
verses.en: [NOTE:1] Now Korah son of Izhar, the son of Kohath, the son of Levi, and Dathan and Abiram, the sons of Eliab, and On son of Peleth, who were Reubenites,[NOTE:2] took men[NOTE:3]
notes: There are three main movements in the story of ch. 16. The first is the rebellion itself (vv. 1-19). The second is the judgment (vv. 20-35). Third is the atonement for the rebels (vv. 36-50). The whole chapter is a marvelous account of a massive rebellion against the leaders that concludes with reconciliation. For further study see G. Hort, “The Death of Qorah,” ABR 7 (1959): 2-26; and J. Liver, “Korah, Dathan and Abiram,” Studies in the Bible (ScrHier 8), 189-217.
The MT reading is plural (“the sons of Reuben”); the Smr and LXX have the singular (“the son of Reuben”).

In the Hebrew text there is no object for the verb “took.” The translation presented above supplies the word “men.” However, it is possible that the MT has suffered damage here. The LXX has “and he spoke.” The Syriac and Targum have “and he was divided.” The editor of BHS suggests that perhaps the MT should be emended to “and he arose.”
verses.commentary:
16:1 "Korah. . ." The full family tree of Korah can be seen in Exod. 6:16-25. Korah and Reuben camped on the
south side of the Tabernacle. This physical proximity may be involved in the explanation of why these two tribes rebelled together.

▣ "On the son of Peleth" It is interesting that three of the descendants of Reuben are mentioned in this
verse. However, On is only mentioned in this verse (cf. Num. 26:4-11).

verses.zh: 并以色列会中的二百五十个首领，就是有名望选入会中的人，在摩西面前一同起来，
verses.en: and rebelled against Moses, along with some of the Israelites, 250 leaders[NOTE:1] of the community, chosen from the assembly,[NOTE:2] famous men.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “princes” (so KJV, ASV).
These men must have been counselors or judges of some kind.
Heb “men of name,” or “men of renown.”
verses.commentary:
16:2 "two hundred and fifty leaders of the congregation, chosen in the assembly, men of renown" This shows
other tribal leaders were also involved in the rebellion against the authority of Moses and Aaron, and not just the rabble of
Num. 11:4. It is ironic that these men, chosen by their peers, were not chosen by God (i.e., 1 Sam. 16:7-10).

▣

NASB, NKJV, LXX, Peshitta
"men of renown"

NRSV
"well-known men"

TEV
"well known leaders"

NJB, JPSOA
"men of repute"

REB
"men of good standing"

The term (BDB 1027, KB 1548, D, #4) basically means "name." Here it denotes

- men of standing or reputation, Ruth 4:11

- men who continue the family name, Gen. 9:14; 25:6-7

- powerful, Gen. 6:4

In this context they were tribal leaders.

verses.zh: 聚集攻击摩西、亚伦，说：「你们擅自专权！全会众个个既是圣洁，耶和华也在他们中间，你们为甚么自高，超过耶和华的会众呢？」
verses.en: And they assembled against Moses and Aaron, saying to them, “You take too much upon yourselves,[NOTE:1] seeing that the whole community is holy, every one of them, and the Lord is among them. Why then do you exalt yourselves above the community of the Lord?”
notes: The meaning of רַב־לָכֶם (rav lakhem) is something like “you have assumed far too much authority.” It simply means “much to you,” perhaps “you have gone to far,” or “you are overreaching yourselves” (M. Noth, Numbers [OTL], 123). He is objecting to the exclusiveness of the system that Moses has been introducing.
verses.commentary:
16:3 "You have gone far enough, for all the congregation are holy, every one of them, and the
Lord is in their midst" This sounds like a really good argument. It sounds like one that
I have made in interpreting Eph. 4:11-12. It does assert a half-truth. It seems that although all of Israel was a kingdom of
priests (cf. Exod. 19:5-6), God chose special leaders out of this group to lead His people. There is a dialectical tension
between all of God's people being priests and God choosing certain leaders among them.

▣ "are holy" Israel is "holy" (see
SPECIAL TOPIC: HOLY) because of their covenant relationship to the "holy" Deity. All things connected to YHWH take
on a sacredness. This is both a possession and a godliness (see
SPECIAL TOPIC: SANCTIFICATION).

▣ "the Lord is in their midst" The people are basing their argument about
being holy on the presence of the Lord in their camp (cf. Lev. 20:12; Num. 5:3; 35:34).

verses.zh: 摩西听见这话就俯伏在地，
verses.en: When Moses heard it he fell down with his face to the ground.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “fell on his face.”
verses.commentary: 16:4 Moses recognized the extent of the rebellion (cf. Num. 14:5). This is just another in a series questioning YHWH.

verses.zh: 对可拉和他一党的人说：「到了早晨，耶和华必指示谁是属他的，谁是圣洁的，就叫谁亲近他；他所拣选的是谁，必叫谁亲近他。
verses.en: Then he said to Korah and to all his company, “In the morning the Lord will make known who are his, and who is holy. He will cause that person[NOTE:1] to approach him; the person he has chosen he will cause to approach him.
notes: Heb “him.”
verses.commentary:
16:5 "even the one whom He will choose" God's choice—not man's is the key. The irony between Num. 16:2
and 5 is obvious.

verses.zh: 可拉啊，你们要这样行，你和你的一党要拿香炉来。
verses.en: Do this, Korah, you and all your company:[NOTE:1] Take censers,
notes: Heb “his congregation” or “his community.” The expression is unusual, but what it signifies is that Korah had set up a rival “Israel” with himself as leader.
verses.commentary:
16:6-7 "Do this: take censers for yourselves, Korah and all your company. . ." Moses proposed an ultimate test.
All of these men would have remembered what happened to Nadab and Abihu in Leviticus 10, when they approached the
Lord with strange fire in their censers. This group would have their day in court but it would be a life-giving confrontation.

Numbers 16:6 and 7 have a series of IMPERATIVES to Korah and his company.

- do this ‒ BDB 793, KB 889, Qal

- take censers ‒ BDB 542, KB 534, Qal

- put fire in them ‒ BDB 678, KB 733, Qal

- lay incense upon them ‒ BDB 962, KB 1321, Qal
There are two more in Num. 16:16-17.

- present before the Lord ‒ BDB 224, KB 243, Qal

- each of you take his firepan ‒ BDB 542, KB 534, Qal

verses.zh: 明日，在耶和华面前，把火盛在炉中，把香放在其上。耶和华拣选谁，谁就为圣洁。你们这利未的子孙擅自专权了！」
verses.en: put fire in them, and set incense on them before the Lord tomorrow, and the man whom the Lord chooses will be holy. You take too much upon yourselves, you sons of Levi!”

verses.zh: 摩西又对可拉说：「利未的子孙哪，你们听我说！
verses.en: Moses said to Korah, “Listen now, you sons of Levi!
verses.commentary: 16:8-10 This is the only clue to the psychological motivation of Korah.

verses.zh: 以色列的　神从以色列会中将你们分别出来，使你们亲近他，办耶和华帐幕的事，并站在会众面前替他们当差。
verses.en: Does it seem too small a thing to you that the God of Israel has separated you from the community of Israel to bring you near to himself, to perform the service of the tabernacle of the Lord, and to stand before the community to minister to them?

verses.zh: 耶和华又使你和你一切弟兄―利未的子孙―一同亲近他，这岂为小事？你们还要求祭司的职任吗？
verses.en: He has brought you near and all your brothers, the sons of Levi, with you. Do you now seek[NOTE:1] the priesthood also?
notes: The verb is the Piel perfect. There is no imperfect tense before this, which makes the construction a little difficult. If the vav (ו) is classified as a consecutive, then the form would stand alone as an equivalent to the imperfect, and rendered as a modal nuance such as “would you [now] seek,” or as a progressive imperfect, “are you seeking.” This latter nuance can be obtained by treating it as a regular perfect tense, with an instantaneous nuance: “do you [now] seek.”sn Moses discerned correctly the real motivation for the rebellion. Korah wanted to be the high priest because he saw how much power there was in the spiritual leadership in Israel. He wanted something like a general election with himself as the candidate and his supporters promoting him. The great privilege of being a Levite and serving in the sanctuary was not enough for him—the status did not satisfy him. Korah gave no rebuttal. The test would be one of ministering with incense. This would bring them into direct proximity with the Lord. If God honored Korah as a ministering priest, then it would be settled. But Moses accuses them of rebellion against the Lord because the Lord had chosen Aaron to be the priest.

verses.zh: 你和你一党的人聚集是要攻击耶和华。亚伦算甚么，你们竟向他发怨言呢？」
verses.en: Therefore you and all your company have assembled together against the Lord! And Aaron—what is he that you murmur against him?”[NOTE:1]
notes: The question indicates that they had been murmuring against Aaron, that is, expressing disloyalty and challenging his leadership. But it is actually against the Lord that they had been murmuring because the Lord had put Aaron in that position.
verses.commentary:
16:11 "gathered together against the Lord" It is interesting that as these people
rebelled against YHWH's rules they were rebelling against Him. We need to hear that today! There must be a balance in
our day between the faithful following of God-given leaders and God-given leaders being more led by God and not by themselves.

verses.zh: 摩西打发人去召以利押的儿子大坍、亚比兰。他们说：「我们不上去！
verses.en: Then Moses summoned[NOTE:1] Dathan and Abiram, the sons of Eliab, but they said, “We will not come up.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “Moses sent to summon.” The verb קָרָא (qaraʾ) followed by the ל (lamed) preposition does not mean “call to” but “summon.” This is a command performance; for them to appear would be to submit to Moses’ authority. This they will not do.

The imperfect tense of נַעֲלֶה (naʿaleh) expresses their unwillingness to report: “we are not willing,” or “we will not.” The verb means “to go up.” It is used in the sense of appearing before an authority or a superior (see, e.g., Gen 46:31; Deut 25:7; Judg 4:5).
verses.commentary:
16:12-14 "Moses sent a summons to Dathan and Abiram, the sons of Eliab" These non-Levite families
of Reuben refused to respond to Moses' summons to come to the same meeting where he confronted Korah.

Their reasons are as follows:

- they accused Moses of taking them out of the land of milk and honey, referring to Egypt

- they are all going to die by warfare in the wilderness

- they did not have the Promised Land allocation

- Moses was "lording it over them" (this is an intensified form; INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE and an
IMPERFECT VERB, both Hithpael)

My, what a lapse of memory they had since the days of hard taskmasters in Egypt! Really, they were not
confronting Moses, but God, in His plan and provisions.

verses.zh: 你将我们从流奶与蜜之地领上来，要在旷野杀我们，这岂为小事？你还要自立为王辖管我们吗？
verses.en: Is it a small thing[NOTE:1] that you have brought us up out of the land that flows with milk and honey,[NOTE:2] to kill us in the wilderness? Now do you want to make yourself a prince[NOTE:3] over us?
notes: The question is rhetorical. It was not a small thing to them—it was a big thing.

The modern scholar who merely sees these words as belonging to an earlier tradition about going up to the land of Canaan that flows with milk and honey misses the irony here. What is happening is that the text is showing how twisted the thinking of the rebels is. They have turned things completely around. Egypt was the land flowing with milk and honey, not Canaan where they will die. The words of rebellion are seldom original, and always twisted.

The verb הִשְׂתָּרֵר (histarer) is the Hitpael infinitive absolute that emphasizes the preceding תִשְׂתָּרֵר (tistarer), the Hitpael imperfect tense (both forms having metathesis). The verb means “to rule; to act like a prince; to make oneself a prince.” This is the only occurrence of the reflexive for this verb. The exact nuance is difficult to translate into English. But they are accusing Moses of seizing princely power for himself, perhaps making a sarcastic reference to his former status in Egypt. The rebels here are telling Moses that they had discerned his scheme, and so he could not “hoodwink” them (cf. NEB).
verses.commentary:
16:13 "Is it not enough" This is a sarcastic, rhetorical question of rebellion (cf. Num. 16:9,13; Josh. 27:17;
Isa. 7:13; Ezek. 16:20; 34:18)

▣ "but you would also lord it over us" This is an Hithpael INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE
and an Hithpael IMPERFECT VERB from the same root, BDB 979, KB 1362, which makes it an
emphatic question. It may be alluding to

- Moses as the only leader of Israel

- Moses' previous status in Pharaoh's court (i.e., "prince")

verses.zh: 并且你没有将我们领到流奶与蜜之地，也没有把田地和葡萄园给我们为业。难道你要剜这些人的眼睛吗？我们不上去！」
verses.en: Moreover,[NOTE:1] you have not brought us into a land that flows with milk and honey, nor given us an inheritance of fields and vineyards. Do you think you can blind[NOTE:2] these men? We will not come up.”
notes: Here אַף (ʾaf) has the sense of “in addition.” It is not a common use.

Heb “will you bore out the eyes of these men?” The question is “Will you continue to mislead them?” (or “hoodwink” them). In Deut 16:19 it is used for taking a bribe; something like that kind of deception is intended here. They are simply stating that Moses is a deceiver who is misleading the people with false promises.
verses.commentary:
16:14

NASB, NKJV, NRSV, Peshitta
"put out the eyes"

TEV
"trying to deceive us"

NJB, REB
"hood-wink"

JPSOA
"gouge out. . .eyes"

LXX
"cut out the eyes"

The Hebrew VERB (BDB 669, KB 722, Piel IMPERFECT)
basically means "to bore out," "pick out" (cf. Pro. 30:17), or "gouge out" (cf. Jdgs. 16:21). Here, it is imagery for tricking
someone about something. They are challenging the integrity and motives of Moses, YHWH's chosen leader.

verses.zh: 摩西就甚发怒，对耶和华说：「求你不要享受他们的供物。我并没有夺过他们一匹驴，也没有害过他们一个人。」
verses.en: Moses was very angry, and he said to the Lord, “Have no respect[NOTE:1] for their offering! I have not taken so much as one donkey from them, nor have I harmed any one of them!”
notes: The verb means “to turn toward”; it is a figurative expression that means “to pay attention to” or “to have regard for.” So this is a prayer against Dathan and Abiram.
verses.commentary:
16:15 Moses has had it with these people.

- he became very angry

- do not regard their offering (i.e., the censers, vv. 6-7)

- he claims he has not taken a single donkey

- he has not harmed any of them in any way (this is similar to Samuel's response in 1 Sam. 22:3 and Nehemiah's response
in Nehemiah 5)

verses.zh: 摩西对可拉说：「明天，你和你一党的人，并亚伦，都要站在耶和华面前；
verses.en: Then Moses said to Korah, “You and all your company present yourselves before the Lord—you and they, and Aaron—tomorrow.

verses.zh: 各人要拿一个香炉，共二百五十个，把香放在上面，到耶和华面前。你和亚伦也各拿自己的香炉。」
verses.en: And each of you[NOTE:1] take his censer, put[NOTE:2] incense in it, and then each of you present his censer before the Lord: 250 censers, along with you, and Aaron—each of you with his censer.”
notes: Heb “and take, a man, his censer.”
This verb and the following one are both perfect tenses with vav (ו) consecutives. Following the imperative they carry the same force, but in sequence.
verses.commentary:
16:17 "two hundred and fifty firepans" There were special firepans for the priests but there would not have been
this many. Obviously these were firepans which were used at home or they were made especially for this occasion. Notice
these non-priests were to approach YHWH's Tabernacle as if they were. Surely they remembered Nadab and Abihu of
Leviticus 10.

verses.zh: 于是他们各人拿一个香炉，盛上火，加上香，同摩西、亚伦站在会幕门前。
verses.en: So everyone took his censer, put fire in it, and set incense on it, and stood at the entrance of the tent of meeting, with Moses and Aaron.

verses.zh: 可拉招聚全会众到会幕门前，要攻击摩西、亚伦；耶和华的荣光就向全会众显现。
verses.en: When[NOTE:1] Korah assembled the whole community against them at the entrance of the tent of meeting, then the glory of the Lord appeared to the whole community.
notes: This clause is clearly foundational for the clause that follows, the appearance of the Lord; therefore it should be subordinated to the next as a temporal clause (one preterite followed by another preterite may be so subordinated).
verses.commentary:
16:19 "the glory of the Lord appeared to all the congregation" See notes at Num. 14:10;
16:42; 20:6.

This represented the personal presence of YHWH.

For "glory" see
SPECIAL TOPIC: GLORY (kabod).

For "Lord" see
SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, D.

verses.zh: 耶和华晓谕摩西、亚伦说：
verses.en: The Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron:

verses.zh: 「你们离开这会众，我好在转眼之间把他们灭绝。」
verses.en: “Separate yourselves[NOTE:1] from among this community,[NOTE:2] that I may consume them in an instant.”
notes: The verb is הִבָּדְלוּ (hibbadelu), the Niphal imperative of בָּדַל (badal). This is the same word that was just used when Moses reminded the Levites that they had been separated from the community to serve the Lord.
The group of people siding with Korah is meant, and not the entire community of the people of Israel. They are an assembly of rebels, their “community” consisting in their common plot.
verses.commentary:
16:21 "Separate yourselves from among this congregation, that I may consume them instantly" Again, this seems
to be another test of Moses (cf. Exod. 32:9,10; Num. 14:11,12; 16:45). YHWH really was attempting to start over with Moses,
as He had with Noah and Abraham.

The VERB "separate" (BDB 95, KB 110, Niphal IMPERATIVE)
basically means "to separate," "to divide," or "to set apart." The NOUN form is used in v. 16 of the Levites
being set apart to the service of the Tabernacle (cf. Num. 8:14; 23:13). Also note:

- to set apart the people of Israel to YHWH, Lev. 20:24,26

- to set apart some Levites for the music ministry, 1 Chr. 25:1

- separate mercenaries from service, 2 Chr. 25:10

- to designate people to bury the dead, Ezek. 39:14

- here (cf. v. 45), it means to "get away from" those about to be judged by YHWH (i.e., the whole people of God); in v. 24,
the same concept is expressed by "get back from. . ."

verses.zh: 摩西、亚伦就俯伏在地，说：「　神，万人之灵的　神啊，一人犯罪，你就要向全会众发怒吗？」
verses.en: Then they threw themselves down with their faces to the ground[NOTE:1] and said, “O God, the God of the spirits of all people,[NOTE:2] will you be angry with the whole community when only one man sins?”[NOTE:3]
notes: It is Moses and Aaron who prostrate themselves; they have the good of the people at heart.

The expression “the God of the spirits of all humanity [flesh]” is somewhat difficult. The Hebrew text says אֱלֹהֵי הָרוּחֹת לְכָל־בָּשָׂר (ʾelohe harukhot lekhol basar). This expression occurs in Num 27:16 again. It also occurs in some postbiblical texts, a fact which has prompted some scholars to conclude that it is a late addition. The words clearly show that Moses is interceding for the congregation. The appeal in the verse is that it is better for one man to die for the whole nation than the whole nation for one man (see also John 11:50).

The verb is the Qal imperfect יֶחֱטָא (yekhetaʾ); it refers to the sinful rebellion of Korah, but Moses is stating something of a principle: “One man sins, and will you be angry….” A past tense translation would assume that this is a preterite use of the imperfect (without vav [ו] consecutive).
verses.commentary:
16:22 "God of the spirits of all flesh" This is a word play on the Hebrew word ruah (BDB 924, cf. Num. 27:16),
which can mean "wind," "breath," or "spirit." It seems to be an allusion to Gen. 2:7. See Special Topics:
SPIRIT IN THE BIBLE and
MONOTHEISM.

▣ "when one man sins, will You be angry with the entire congregation" It is obvious from the earlier
parts of the OT that corporate responsibility is emphasized (i.e., Adam's sin, Genesis 3; Achan's sin, Joshua 7). However,
in verses such as this, one begins to see an ancient form of individualism being manifested. Compare Jer. 31:31-34 and
Ezekiel 18 for a continuing emphasis on individual responsibility (cf. Matt. 10:32; John 1:12; 3:16; Rom. 10:9-13).

16:22-29 These verses record Moses' words about the coming judgment on the rebels and their families.

He asserts that if they die a natural death, then he has not been sent by YHWH.

He also asserts that this judgment is not something he wanted (v. 28). Judgment is always a tragedy!
YHWH is a gracious God but He is also a "holy" and "righteous" God. There are consequences to rebellion and disobedience.
See the Special Topics:

-
CHARACTERISTICS OF ISRAEL'S GOD (OT)

- HOLY

- RIGHTEOUSNESS

- JUDGMENT IN THE NT

verses.zh: 耶和华晓谕摩西说：
verses.en: So the Lord spoke to Moses:

verses.zh: 「你吩咐会众说：『你们离开可拉、大坍、亚比兰帐棚的四围。』」
verses.en: “Tell the community: ‘Get away[NOTE:1] from around the homes of Korah, Dathan, and Abiram.’”
notes: The motif of “going up” is still present; here the Hebrew text says “go up” (the Niphal imperative—“go up yourselves”) from their tents, meaning, move away from them.

verses.zh: 摩西起来，往大坍、亚比兰那里去；以色列的长老也随着他去。
verses.en: Then Moses got up[NOTE:1] and went to Dathan and Abiram; and the elders of Israel went after him.
notes: Heb “rose up.”

verses.zh: 他吩咐会众说：「你们离开这恶人的帐棚吧，他们的物件，甚么都不可摸，恐怕你们陷在他们的罪中，与他们一同消灭。」
verses.en: And he said to the community, “Move away from the tents of these wicked[NOTE:1] men, and do not touch anything they have, lest you be destroyed because[NOTE:2] of all their sins.”[NOTE:3]
notes: The word רָשָׁע (rashaʿ) has the sense of a guilty criminal. The word “wicked” sometimes gives the wrong connotation. These men were opposing the Lord, and so were condemned as criminals—they were guilty. The idea of “wickedness” therefore applies in that sense.
The preposition ב (bet) in this line is causal—“on account of their sins.”

The impression is that the people did not hear what the Lord said to Moses, but only what Moses said to the people as a result. They saw the brilliant cloud, and perhaps heard the sound of his voice, but the relaying of the instructions indicates they did not hear the actual instruction from the Lord himself.
verses.commentary:
16:26 "touch nothing that belongs to them" Apparently these men were treated as Jericho will be later in the
sense of herem (see SPECIAL TOPIC:
CURSE IN THE OT) or "holy war" as that which is uniquely dedicated to God. It becomes so holy that it cannot be used
by humans.

verses.zh: 于是众人离开可拉、大坍、亚比兰帐棚的四围。大坍、亚比兰带着妻子、儿女、小孩子，都出来，站在自己的帐棚门口。
verses.en: So they got away from the homes of Korah, Dathan, and Abiram on every side, and Dathan and Abiram came out and stationed themselves[NOTE:1] in the entrances of their tents with their wives, their children, and their toddlers.
notes: The verb נִצָּבִים (nitsavim) suggests a defiant stance, for the word is often used in the sense of taking a stand for or against something. It can also be somewhat neutral, having the sense of positioning oneself for a purpose.

verses.zh: 摩西说：「我行的这一切事本不是凭我自己心意行的，乃是耶和华打发我行的，必有证据使你们知道。
verses.en: Then Moses said, “This is how[NOTE:1] you will know that the Lord has sent me to do all these works, for I have not done them of my own will.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “in this.”

The Hebrew text simply has כִּי־לֹא מִלִּבִּי (ki loʾ millibbi, “for not from my heart”). The heart is the center of the will, the place decisions are made (see H. W. Wolff, Anthropology of the Old Testament). Moses is saying that the things he has done have not come “from the will of man” so to speak—and certainly not from some secret desire on his part to seize power.
verses.commentary:
16:28 "this is not my doing" Literally, "not from my heart." The exodus and the events that followed were
not at Moses' direction and surely not a plan by him to grab power over Israel.

verses.zh: 这些人死若与世人无异，或是他们所遭的与世人相同，就不是耶和华打发我来的。
verses.en: If these men die a natural death,[NOTE:1] or if they share the fate[NOTE:2] of all men, then the Lord has not sent me.
notes: Heb “if like the death of every man they die.”
The noun is פְּקֻדָּה (pequddah, “appointment, visitation”). The expression refers to a natural death, parallel to the first expression.

verses.zh: 倘若耶和华创作一件新事，使地开口，把他们和一切属他们的都吞下去，叫他们活活地坠落阴间，你们就明白这些人是藐视耶和华了。」
verses.en: But if the Lord does something entirely new,[NOTE:1] and the earth opens its mouth and swallows them up[NOTE:2] along with all that they have, and they[NOTE:3] go down alive to the grave,[NOTE:4] then you will know that these men have despised the Lord!”
notes: The verb בָּרָא (baraʾ) is normally translated “create” in the Bible. More specifically it means to fashion or make or do something new and fresh. Here the verb is joined with its cognate accusative to underscore that this will be so different everyone will know it is of God.
The figures are personifications, but they vividly describe the catastrophe to follow—which was very much like a mouth swallowing them.

The word is “life” or “lifetime”; it certainly means their lives—they themselves. But the presence of this word suggests more. It is an accusative specifying the state of the subject—they will go down alive to Sheol.

The word “Sheol” in the Bible can be used four different ways: the grave, the realm of the departed [wicked] spirits or Hell, death in general, or a place of extreme danger (one that will lead to the grave if God does not intervene). The usage here is certainly the first, and very likely the second as well. A translation of “pit” would not be inappropriate. Since they will go down there alive, it is likely that they will sense the deprivation and the separation from the land above. See H. W. Robinson, Inspiration and Revelation in the Old Testament; N. J. Tromp, Primitive Conceptions of Death and the Netherworld in the Old Testament (BibOr 21), 21-23; and A. Heidel, The Gilgamesh Epic, especially ch. 3.
verses.commentary:
16:30 "the Lord brings about an entirely new thing. . .descend alive into Sheol" Moses
prophesies a test (like Aaron's rod of Numbers 17). He says that if these men die a natural death, then he is not a prophet and
God has not chosen him, but if the earth opens up and uniquely swallows this group (i.e., a personification of Num. 26:10;
Deut. 11:6; Ps. 106:16-18, cf. Exod. 15:12), then God has confirmed Moses' and Aaron's leadership. The ancient Hebrews
believed that the earth contained the dead because that is where they placed their dead (see
SPECIAL TOPIC: WHERE ARE
THE DEAD?). This is not a scientific explanation but is simply a metaphor of description (i.e., phenomenological language),
which is common in the OT.

There is some confusion about how Korah died. Was Korah with this group of Reubenites or was he
one of those who offered fire before the Lord in the Tabernacle? It seems, from Num. 26:11-12, that Korah left the two
hundred and fifty in the Tabernacle and went to stand with the sons of Reuben and was, thereby, swallowed up along with
them, as was his family.

▣

NASB
"brings about an entirely new thing"

NKJV, NRSV
"creates"

TEV, JPSOA
"does something unheard of"

NJB
"does something utterly new"

REB
"works a miracle"

LXX
"show forth by an omen"

Peshitta
"make a new thing"

This is the Hebrew VERB bara (BDB 135, KB 153, Qal
IMPERFECT accompanied by its NOUN). The VERB is used in
Gen. 1:1 (a Qal PERFECT). It is used only of Divine activity. However, here, it is not "out
of nothing" (i.e., ex nihilo) but something never done before using existing natural features.

I personally am not sure that Genesis specifically asserts creation out of nothing. Remember, Genesis
1-2 is an abbreviated summary of YHWH's activity over time. It asserts the "who" and "why," not the "how" and "when" of
creation. See full notes online at Genesis 1-2. See Millard Erickson, Christian Theology, 2 ed., pp. 394-397, and
NIDOTTE, vol. 1, pp. 728-234.

verses.zh: 摩西刚说完了这一切话，他们脚下的地就开了口，
verses.en: When he had finished[NOTE:1] speaking[NOTE:2] all these words, the ground that was under them split open,
notes: The initial temporal clause is standard: It begins with the temporal indicator “and it was,” followed here by the Piel infinitive construct with the preposition and the subjective genitive suffix. “And it happened when he finished.”
The infinitive construct with the preposition ל (lamed) functions here as the direct object of the preceding infinitive. It tells what he finished.

verses.zh: 把他们和他们的家眷，并一切属可拉的人丁、财物，都吞下去。
verses.en: and the earth opened its mouth and swallowed them, along with their households, and all Korah’s men, and all their goods.

verses.zh: 这样，他们和一切属他们的，都活活地坠落阴间；地口在他们上头照旧合闭，他们就从会中灭亡。
verses.en: They and all that they had went down alive into the pit, and the earth closed over them. So they perished from among the community.

verses.zh: 在他们四围的以色列众人听他们呼号，就都逃跑，说：「恐怕地也把我们吞下去。」
verses.en: All the Israelites[NOTE:1] who were around them fled at their cry,[NOTE:2] for they said, “What if[NOTE:3] the earth swallows us too?”
notes: Heb “all Israel.”
Heb “voice.”
Heb “lest.”
verses.commentary:
16:34-35 Here we see that all the rebellious leaders of Korah's group who wanted to be priests were killed
instantaneously by fire (see SPECIAL TOPIC:
FIRE). This is similar to what occurred in Leviticus 10.

There is some ambiguity here because of the use of the number "two hundred and fifty." Some say it
refers to the tribal leaders of v. 2, while others say it refers to two hundred members of Korah's own family who wanted to
be priests.

For a good discussion on "Judgment" see Dictionary of Biblical Imagery, pp. 470-474.

verses.zh: 又有火从耶和华那里出来，烧灭了那献香的二百五十个人。
verses.en: Then a fire[NOTE:1] went out from the Lord and devoured the 250 men who offered incense.
notes: For a discussion of the fire of the Lord, see J. C. H. Laughlin, “The Strange Fire of Nadab and Abihu,” JBL 95 (1976): 559-65.

verses.zh: 耶和华晓谕摩西说：
verses.en: (17:1)[NOTE:1] The Lord spoke to Moses:
notes: Beginning with 16:36, the verse numbers through 17:13 in the English Bible differ from the verse numbers in the Hebrew text (BHS), with 16:36 ET = 17:1 HT, 16:37 ET = 17:2 HT, 17:1 ET = 17:16 HT, etc., through 17:13 ET = 17:28 HT. With 18:1 the verse numbers in the ET and HT are again the same. But in the English chap. 17 there are two parts: Aaron’s rod budding (1-9), and the rod preserved as a memorial (10-13). Both sections begin with the same formula.
verses.commentary:
16:36-40 The MT starts chapter 17 at v. 36 (cf. NJB versing). The firepans of the rebel Levites were to be kept
because they were holy. They became a new bronze (cf. Exod. 27:3) covering for the sacrificial altar. This would be a sign
for the children of Israel. God's acts of judgment were meant to teach later generations. They had to be recorded as accurately
as His acts of grace (cf. Num. 17:10). See Special Topics:

- ALTAR OF SACRIFICE

- ALTAR OF INCENSE

verses.zh: 「你吩咐祭司亚伦的儿子以利亚撒从火中捡起那些香炉来，把火撒在别处，因为那些香炉是圣的。
verses.en: “Tell[NOTE:1] Eleazar son of Aaron the priest to pick up[NOTE:2] the censers out of the flame, for they are holy, and then scatter the coals of fire[NOTE:3] at a distance.
notes: Heb “say to.”
The verb is the jussive with a vav (ו) coming after the imperative; it may be subordinated to form a purpose clause (“that he may pick up”) or the object of the imperative.
The Hebrew text just has “fire,” but it would be hard to conceive of this action apart from the idea of coals of fire.

verses.zh: 把那些犯罪、自害己命之人的香炉，叫人锤成片子，用以包坛。那些香炉本是他们在耶和华面前献过的，所以是圣的，并且可以给以色列人作记号。」
verses.en: As for the censers of these men who sinned at the cost of their lives,[NOTE:1] they must be made[NOTE:2] into hammered sheets for covering the altar, because they presented them before the Lord and sanctified them. They will become a sign to the Israelites.”
notes: The expression is “in/by/against their life.” That they sinned against their life means that they brought ruin to themselves.
The form is the perfect tense with vav (ו) consecutive. But there is no expressed subject for “and they shall make them,” and so it may be treated as a passive (“they shall [must] be made”).

verses.zh: 于是祭司以利亚撒将被烧之人所献的铜香炉拿来，人就锤出来，用以包坛，
verses.en: So Eleazar the priest took the bronze censers presented by those who had been burned up, and they were hammered out as a covering for the altar.

verses.zh: 给以色列人作纪念，使亚伦后裔之外的人不得近前来在耶和华面前烧香，免得他遭可拉和他一党所遭的。这乃是照耶和华藉着摩西所吩咐的。
verses.en: It was a memorial for the Israelites, that no outsider who is not a descendant of[NOTE:1] Aaron should approach to burn incense before the Lord, that he might not become like Korah and his company—just as the Lord had spoken by the authority[NOTE:2] of Moses.
notes: Heb “from the seed of.”
Heb “hand.”

verses.zh: 第二天，以色列全会众都向摩西、亚伦发怨言说：「你们杀了耶和华的百姓了。」
verses.en: But on the next day the whole community of Israelites murmured against Moses and Aaron, saying, “You have killed the Lord’s people!”[NOTE:1]
notes: The whole congregation here is trying to project its guilt on Moses and Aaron. It was they and their rebellion that brought about the deaths, not Moses and Aaron. The Lord had punished the sinners. The fact that the leaders had organized a rebellion against the Lord was forgotten by these people. The point here is that the Israelites had learned nothing of spiritual value from the event.
verses.commentary:
16:41 "all the congregation of the sons of Israel grumbled against Moses and Aaron" One would think
that the actions of God, His judgment against those who rebelled, would preclude the people of God from
grumbling so soon. Unfortunately, it did not! Fallen human nature is pervasive and recurrent.

verses.zh: 会众聚集攻击摩西、亚伦的时候，向会幕观看，不料，有云彩遮盖了，耶和华的荣光显现。
verses.en: When the community assembled[NOTE:1] against Moses and Aaron, they turned toward the tent of meeting—and[NOTE:2] the cloud covered it, and the glory of the Lord appeared.
notes: The temporal clause is constructed with the temporal indicator (“and it was”) followed by the Niphal infinitive construct and preposition.

The verse uses וְהִנֵּה (vehinneh, “and behold”). This is the deictic particle—it is used to point things out, suddenly calling attention to them, as if the reader were there. The people turned to look toward the tent—and there is the cloud!

verses.zh: 摩西、亚伦就来到会幕前。
verses.en: Then Moses and Aaron stood before the tent of meeting.

verses.zh: 耶和华吩咐摩西说：
verses.en: The Lord spoke to Moses:

verses.zh: 「你们离开这会众，我好在转眼之间把他们灭绝。」他们二人就俯伏于地。
verses.en: “Get away from this community, so that I can consume them in an instant!” But they threw themselves down with their faces to the ground.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “they fell on their faces.”

verses.zh: 摩西对亚伦说：「拿你的香炉，把坛上的火盛在其中，又加上香，快快带到会众那里，为他们赎罪；因为有忿怒从耶和华那里出来，瘟疫已经发作了。」
verses.en: Then Moses said to Aaron, “Take the censer, put burning coals from the altar in it, place incense on it, and go quickly into the assembly and make atonement for them, for wrath has gone out from the Lord—the plague has begun!”
verses.commentary:
16:46 "the plague has begun" Here is a dramatic example of the intermediary effectiveness of Aaron,
God's special choice as priest. Aaron stood between the plague and the tribes of Israel who were still alive
and effectively placated the wrath of God. This is the only account in all the Pentateuch where offering
incense acted in the sense of atonement. Another unusual text is Num. 31:50, where the Israelites made an
offering of gold jewelry to make atonement. Usually it required a blood sacrifice.

▣ Notice the number of IMPERATIVES.

- take your censer ‒ BDB 542, KB 534, Qal IMPERATIVE

- put fire in it ‒ BDB 678, KB 733, Qal IMPERATIVE

- lay incense on it ‒ BDB 962, KB 1321, Qal IMPERATIVE

- bring it quickly ‒ BDB 229, KB 246, Hiphil IMPERATIVE

- make atonement ‒ BDB 497, KB 493, Piel IMPERATIVE; see
SPECIAL TOPIC: ATONEMENT

Normally, Moses intercedes for Israel but in this case, Aaron offers a sacrifice of incense (only here
in the OT) to stay YHWH's hand of judgment.

This had to happen quickly (i.e., "Aaron ran," v. 47). Normally, priests had to avoid the dead but here
Aaron ran to the demarcation between the living and the dead.

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary which means that you are responsible for your own
interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation.
You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this section of
the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

- How are the family of Levites from Kohath in contact with a family of the tribe of Reuben?

- Are all Israelites "holy"? If so, how?

- How are Leviticus 10 and Numbers 16 related?

- What did Korah want?

- What did the family of Reubenites want?

- How is Num. 16:22 related to Ezekiel 18?

- Define "Sheol."

- How does the concept of "Hebrew corporality" affect the families of the rebels?

- Why were the censers holy?

- What is unique about Num. 16:46?

verses.zh: 亚伦照着摩西所说的拿来，跑到会中，不料，瘟疫在百姓中已经发作了。他就加上香，为百姓赎罪。
verses.en: So Aaron did[NOTE:1] as Moses commanded[NOTE:2] and ran into the middle of the assembly, where the plague was just beginning among the people. So he placed incense on the coals and made atonement for the people.
notes: Heb “took.”
Or “had spoken” (NASB); NRSV “had ordered.”

verses.zh: 他站在活人死人中间，瘟疫就止住了。
verses.en: He stood between the dead and the living, and the plague was stopped.

verses.zh: 除了因可拉事情死的以外，遭瘟疫死的，共有一万四千七百人。
verses.en: Now 14,700 people died in the plague, in addition to those who died in the event with Korah.

verses.zh: 亚伦回到会幕门口，到摩西那里，瘟疫已经止住了。
verses.en: Then Aaron returned to Moses at the entrance of the tent of meeting, and the plague was stopped.

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own
interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation.
You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects. Compare your subject divisions with the five translations
above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation.
Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

- First paragraph

BACKGROUND STUDY

- Although the text does not specifically mention the motives for the rebellion, one is tempted to see jealousy as the
primary factor (cf. Num. 11:2).

- Korah, a member of the family of Levites who had the unique responsibility of carrying the furniture of the Tabernacle,
wanted to share leadership with Aaron (cf. Num. 16:8-10). This shows the tension between the priests and the Levites,
all descendants of Levi.

- Reuben, the firstborn of Jacob, seemingly wanted to have a share of the preeminence he had lost.

- The rebellion was somewhat more widely spread than just the family of Korah and three of the sons of Reuben. We see
that there were over 250 leaders of the different tribes who were involved in this particular rebellion. This shows the extent
of the unrest and lack of confidence among the people of God. See Josephus, Antiq, 4.2.1-4; 4.3.1-4.

- What bothers me personally about OT accounts such as this is whether these people who challenged Moses' and Aaron's
leadership are excluded from heaven or just taken early. Going to Sheol at death (i.e., into the earth; see
SPECIAL TOPIC: SHEOL)
is the lot of all humans since Genesis 3. See
SPECIAL TOPIC: APOSTASY.
